newsitem.title: UK: Copper industry annual deals in melting pot.
newsitem.headline: Copper industry annual deals in melting pot.

text.p: Copper miners and smelters meeting to discuss annual treatment terms are grappling with the likelihood that the current tight concentrates market may look different by the start of 1997.
Treatment and refining charges agreed now may not reflect the supply/demand picture in 1997 -- hence the cautious approach in so-called mating season talks, industry sources said.
The LME annual dinner in October signals the start of talks between producers and refiners. Indications suggest producers and refiners are some $20/tonne and two cents/lb apart.
Negotations began a few weeks ago in Tokyo between Japanese smelters and Far Eastern producers, and then moved to London during LME week.

Miners have opened up by looking to lock in annual deals at $90/95 a tonne TC (treatment charge) and 9.0/9.5 cents/lb RC (refining costs), based on price participation (PP) 10 percent above or below 90 cents/lb.
Smelters have responded with proposals of $115/119 for TCs and 11.0/11.5 cents/lb for RCs.
"At the moment miners and smelters are cautious as nobody wants to set a precedent," one industry source said.
The smelters' first response suggests mid-point agreement at $105/tonne and 10.5 cents/lb, Peter Hollands of industry analysts Bloomsbury Mineral Economics (BME) said.
Although there is a smelter bottleneck at present, this will undoubtedly change by the start of 1997, when a large cathode surplus will be building.
Extra high quality electrowon cathode will hit the market early next year from El Abra in Chile, with significant amounts of extra smelter capacity elsewhere also coming on stream.
This will allow surplus concentrates to be converted into extra cathodes.
By January, the Garfield smelter in the U.S., Sterlite's Indian plant and the expanded La Caridad facility in Mexico will all contribute to increased refining capacity, they said.
"By the first quarter of 1997 the concentrate, blister and cathode markets will all be in surplus," Hollands said.
A recent spot concentrate tender went at $120/tonne and 12 cents/lb, although there was no PP. On the spot merchant market business has ranged between $110/115/tonne and 10.5/11.0.
Hollands said the eventual outcome and benchmark level of annual TC/RC terms depended on timing.

"BME predicts that an early settlement will be around $105/tonne and 10.5 cents/lb. If they (negotiations) drag on until January terms will scatter between $100 and $105 a tonne and 10.0 and 10.5 cents," he said.
